title: Public-Sector Contact Center Advisor
summary: An internal web service that helps public-sector contact-center agents follow live STT transcription during a call, then review AI analysis and consultation history after it ends. I designed and implemented the frontend across agent and manager workflows.

keyOutcome.label: Key Outcome
keyOutcome.value: Used by 60% of agents, with average customer wait time reduced by 30%

projectIntro.title: Project overview
projectIntro.description:
I designed and implemented the agent and administrator screens. The workflow connects active-call detection, live speaker-specific transcripts, call and connection status, post-call AI analysis, and consultation history. Agent feedback informed the addition of history search, favorites, and dedicated tabs.

I displayed partial transcripts in temporary areas for each speaker and kept finalized transcripts in start-time order without duplicates. I verified that finalized transcripts survive connection loss and that retries or manual reconnection restore the current state from a fresh snapshot. I also checked that polling and SSE start and stop as calls move between idle, active, and ended states.

multiTabAuth.title: Coordinating inactivity logout and token refresh across tabs
multiTabAuth.description: The project required logout after 15 minutes of inactivity to avoid leaving consultation data exposed in an unattended browser. I coordinated activity timing and logout across tabs, and addressed refresh races that could incorrectly terminate a session.

problem.title: Problem
problem.description: When several tabs received 401 responses together, each tried to refresh with the same single-use Refresh Token. After one tab consumed it, the others retried with an already-used token, received 401 responses, and could propagate logout to otherwise valid tabs.

firstAttempt.title: First decision and its limitation
firstAttempt.description: I first serialized refresh requests with Web Locks. This prevented simultaneous use of the same token, but tabs that acquired the lock in sequence could still make repeated server requests and rotate the Refresh Token unnecessarily.

refreshOwnership.title: One owner for server refresh
refreshOwnership.description: Web Locks serialize server refresh requests. The authentication channel distributes the new Access Token, and receiving tabs adopt it without another request. Serialization does not itself coalesce all waiting requests into a single server call.

resultSharing.title: Sharing refresh results without restoring a logged-out session
resultSharing.description: The authentication channel shares logout events and refreshed Access Tokens. Receiving tabs check logout state and compare exp values before adopting newer tokens. Once logout begins, refresh requests and token adoption are blocked. Refresh Tokens are not broadcast.

verification.title: Outcome and verification
verification.description: Tests verify that receiving tabs adopt a new Access Token without a server request and ignore missing payloads, tokens received during logout, and older expirations. Network and 5xx failures are also separated from invalid authentication so temporary outages do not expand into cross-tab logout.

securityBackground.title: Inactivity logout across tabs
securityBackground.description: Independent timers can log out an active user or leave another tab displaying an ended session. Fifteen minutes was the project policy; the current implementation reads the timeout from server configuration and pauses inactivity timing during a live call.

idleSync.title: Synchronizing activity and propagating logout
idleSync.description: react-idle-timer coordinates activity and timers using crossTab, leaderElection, and syncTimers. The leader handles the server request for inactivity logout. Tabs receiving logged-out on a separate authentication BroadcastChannel clear tokens and query caches, then navigate to the login page.

flow.title: I separated ownership of multi-tab token refresh from result distribution.
flow.description: Activity timing and logout are synchronized across tabs for the project's 15-minute inactivity policy. The diagram below focuses on token refresh: Web Locks coordinate refresh work and BroadcastChannel distributes the refreshed Access Token.

flow.caption: IdleTimer uses its own channel for activity synchronization. A separate authentication channel carries logout and refreshed tokens; tabs that are logging out do not adopt incoming tokens.
